jobs.title: Senior BI/Data Engineer
jobs.description: Your Role in Our Story:  As a Senior BI/Data Engineer at ACT, you will play a key role in modernizing and scaling our enterprise Data Platform. Combining hands-on engineering with technical ownership, you will design reliable, scalable data solutions across data integration, modelling, analytics engineering and platform architecture. Beyond delivery, you will help shape our platform roadmap and engineering standards, with a focus on architecture, automation, performance, security and cost efficiency. Microsoft Fabric is an important part of our modernization journey, alongside technologies such as Databricks where they add value. You will also have the opportunity to explore practical applications of Generative AI across development, documentation and platform operations. We value ownership, collaboration, knowledge sharing and continuous improvement. In essence, your role involves: Own and continuously improve key components of ACT’s Data Platform architecture and engineering standards. Design and implement integrations for new source systems and build reliable, maintainable data pipelines. Design, implement and document enterprise data models, including relational and dimensional models. Develop, optimize and operate data pipelines and orchestration using technologies such as Azure Data Factory, Microsoft Fabric, Azure Functions and Logic Apps. Plan and execute data migrations with appropriate validation, reconciliation, data-quality controls and operational monitoring. Contribute to the modernization of the Data Platform using Microsoft Fabric and, where appropriate, Databricks and other modern data technologies. Develop and maintain trusted semantic models that enable scalable Power BI reporting, analytics and emerging AI use cases. Translate business requirements into sustainable technical solutions and communicate design choices clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders. We are a tech-driven on-demand mobility service that supports our hyper-local communities, helping them thrive and so much more! Develop and optimise SQL transformations, stored procedures and Kimball-style star-schema data models. Build and support Power BI semantic models and the datasets behind dashboards used by teams across the business. Implement data quality, validation and reconciliation checks so numbers match across systems. Monitor production pipelines and troubleshoot data, performance and refresh issues. jobs.title: Data Scientist (Measurement & Signal Processing) (f/m/d)
jobs.description: Description QuantumDiamonds is a novel equipment vendor from Germany which builds magnetic field imaging systems based on quantum sensors. Our Data Science & Machine Learning team in Pre-Development owns the chain from raw quantum sensor data to the current map an engineer can act on: the statistical evaluation of the sensor signal, the simulation and training data pipelines, the reconstruction of fields and currents, with the machine learning pipeline for three-dimensional current in production today, and the validation of every map against simulation and reference measurements. We are looking for a Data Scientist to own one question for the team: can we trust this map, and if not, where in the chain did it go wrong? Every measurement, in our lab or at a customer, gets a verdict and a reason. You build the checks that produce it, keep the catalogue of known artifacts and reference measurements behind it, and make it automatic for the routine cases so that your judgement goes to the hard ones. When a check fails, you trace it to its source in the chain, fix it when it sits in the evaluation, and drive the fix with the owning engineer when it does not. Our Applications engineers, who run the customer projects, rely on your verdict for what reaches the customer. A senior data scientist on the team backs you on the hard calls at the start; the aim is that you become the owner of this question. This is a hands-on analysis role, not a research position: the data is real, the chain is in daily use, and every improvement you make shows up in the next measurement. Your background does not need to be in quantum sensing or semiconductors: if you have learned to tell signal from noise, calibration errors and artifacts in another demanding measurement system, we want to hear from you.
